thingsToDo.title: Huliheʻe Palace
thingsToDo.description: Huliheʻe Palace is a historic palace museum in or near Kailua-Kona, Hawaii. Huliheʻe Palace in Kailua-Kona is a former royal vacation residence built in 1838 and now operated as a museum. The building preserves architecture and furnishings associated with Hawaiian monarchy history on Hawaiʻi Island's Kona coast. The site is regularly referenced in statewide historical, environmental, or cultural documentation. Its present-day access and management context shape how residents and visitors use the area.

thingsToDo.title: Mokuʻaikaua Church
thingsToDo.description: Mokuʻaikaua Church is a historic church in or near Kailua-Kona, Hawaii. Mokuʻaikaua Church in Kailua-Kona, completed in 1837, is considered the oldest Christian church in continuous use in Hawaiʻi. Built with coral-lime mortar and local stone, it reflects early missionary-era religious and civic development in Kona. The site is regularly referenced in statewide historical, environmental, or cultural documentation. Its present-day access and management context shape how residents and visitors use the area.

thingsToDo.title: Kamakahonu
thingsToDo.description: Kamakahonu is a historic royal residence site in or near Kailua-Kona, Hawaii. Kamakahonu is a historic site in Kailua-Kona that served as the residence compound of Kamehameha I in his final years. The area includes Ahuʻena Heiau and is central to interpretations of early nineteenth-century Hawaiian governance. The site is regularly referenced in statewide historical, environmental, or cultural documentation. Its present-day access and management context shape how residents and visitors use the area.

thingsToDo.title: Kaloko-Honokōhau National Historical Park
thingsToDo.description: Kaloko-Honokōhau National Historical Park is a national historical park in or near Kailua-Kona, Hawaii. Kaloko-Honokōhau National Historical Park preserves coastal archaeological sites north of Kailua-Kona, including fishponds, heiau, and ancient settlement features. The park documents traditional Hawaiian aquaculture and shoreline land use in the Kona district. The site is regularly referenced in statewide historical, environmental, or cultural documentation. Its present-day access and management context shape how residents and visitors use the area.

thingsToDo.title: Kailua Pier
thingsToDo.description: Kailua Pier is a oceanfront pier in or near Kailua-Kona, Hawaii. Kailua Pier fronts Kailua-Kona's historic waterfront and functions as a public embarkation and event site. The pier area links former royal grounds, mission-era landmarks, and modern ocean access used for regional recreation and races. The site is regularly referenced in statewide historical, environmental, or cultural documentation. Its present-day access and management context shape how residents and visitors use the area.

faq.q: How many days should I plan for Kailua-Kona?
faq.a: Two to three days is enough for core Kailua-Kona highlights plus one or two local experiences.

faq.q: Should I book tours ahead in Kailua-Kona?
faq.a: Yes—advance booking is recommended for weekends, holidays, and top-rated operators.
